options.content:
Use this dashboard from top to bottom. First select `model`, then check User Health to see whether clients are protected. Next pick the largest bounded `reason`, then use participant-address tables to find which `participant_key` is responsible. Only after the address-level view is clear should you open escrow and host diagnostics.

Authoritative participant panels use gateway-owned metric families with `participant_key` and `model`. Rows marked diagnostic use gateway-wide, escrow, remote-address, or `host_idx` metrics. Those panels explain routing or timing symptoms, but they do not replace participant scoring.

Empty data usually means Prometheus cannot scrape `devshard-gateway`, the gateway image predates these metrics, no `/v1/chat/completions` traffic hit the selected range, or the selected filters exclude the traffic.

panels.description: 1 means Prometheus can scrape the gateway. 0 or no data means the rest of this dashboard is not trustworthy yet.
panels.title: Gateway Scrape

panels.description: Average gateway request rate across the selected time range. This is selected-window volume divided by the selected range duration.
panels.title: Average Request Rate

panels.description: Successful or cached user requests divided by all gateway requests across the selected time range.
panels.title: Range User Success Rate

panels.description: User-visible failures across the selected time range. Drill into the adjacent reason panel before changing protocol parameters.
panels.title: Range Critical User Failures

panels.description: Cached requests divided by all gateway requests across the selected time range. A high value means users are protected by cached output, but winner attribution may be incomplete.
panels.title: Range Cache Hit Share

panels.description: Current gateway-wide capacity scale used to reduce effective limiter caps. 1 means full configured capacity.
panels.title: Gateway Capacity Scale

panels.description: Lowest current capacity scale among selected models. This is the fastest way to spot a model with reduced usable capacity.
panels.title: Worst Model Capacity Scale

panels.description: Final user outcomes grouped by bounded reason. Use this to decide whether user-visible problems are transport, policy, runtime, or request-shape issues.
panels.title: What Users Saw by Outcome and Reason

panels.description: Top user-visible failure reasons in the selected range. Pick one of these in `reason` before inspecting participant and slot rows.
panels.title: Top User-Visible Failure Reasons

panels.description: Gateway-wide HTTP route p95 from the existing route histogram. This is not model-aware and must not be read as participant latency.
panels.title: HTTP Chat Route p95 (gateway-wide)

panels.description: Gateway limiter rejections by bounded reason. This is gateway-wide admission pressure and does not identify a participant address.
panels.title: Gateway Admission Rejections by Reason (gateway-wide)

panels.description: Current limiter load and effective caps after capacity scaling. Rising in-flight values near caps explain gateway-limited outcomes.
panels.title: Active Requests and Input Tokens

panels.description: Real upstream sends by role and reason. Extra attempts are the immediate cost of redundancy and fallback.
panels.title: Real Attempts Started by Role and Reason

panels.description: How real attempts terminated. Visibility separates user-visible winners, suppressed losers, no-winner attempts, and unfinished failures.
panels.title: Terminal Attempts by Outcome and Visibility

panels.description: Failed attempts with reason and visibility preserved. Select a high-volume reason before moving to Participant Quality.
panels.title: Failed Attempts by Reason and Visibility

panels.description: Share of attributed user-visible wins by participant and model across the selected range. Cached requests are excluded unless the gateway can safely attribute the source winner.
panels.title: User-Visible Winner Share by Participant

panels.description: Gateway-wide real sends divided by user requests. Values above 1 mean redundancy or recovery is spending extra participant work.
panels.title: Global Sent Attempts per User Request

panels.description: Gateway-wide failed or not-finished sent attempts divided by successful user requests. Use participant companion tables to find responsible addresses.
panels.title: Global Failed Sends per Successful User Request

panels.description: Diagnostic only: receipt p95 is keyed by `devshard_id` and escrow-local `host_idx`, not participant address. Use it for timeout-window tuning only.
panels.title: Host Receipt p95 by devshard_id and host_idx (diagnostic)

panels.description: Diagnostic only: first-token p95 is keyed by `devshard_id` and `host_idx`, not participant address. Future participant-key first-content metrics should replace this for scoring.
panels.title: Host First Token p95 by devshard_id and host_idx (diagnostic)

panels.description: Diagnostic only: prefill-after-receipt time per input token from host-side metrics. This is not user-visible TTFT.
panels.title: Host Prefill per Input Token p95 by host_idx (diagnostic)

panels.description: Diagnostic only: total attempt time by `devshard_id` and `host_idx`. Use with timeout rows to tune windows.
panels.title: Host Total Attempt Time p95 by devshard_id and host_idx (diagnostic)

panels.description: Successful user requests that hid participant or policy failures. Severity separates protected pre-winner failures from later winner problems.
panels.title: Hidden User Successes by Severity and Reason

panels.description: Suppressed loser failures by reason. These did not reach the user but still consumed participant work.
panels.title: Hidden Loser Failures by Reason

panels.description: User-visible winner attempts that also recorded a failure reason. Investigate these first because users may have seen partial content or degraded streams.
panels.title: Winner Failures After User-Visible Content

panels.description: Use the `Localized Failure Drilldowns` row for participant-level failure counts and rates. Keeping that drilldown in one place avoids two tables with the same metric and different names.

options.content:
Participant failure drilldowns live in `Localized Failure Drilldowns`:

1. Use `Top Participant Failure Rates by Model` to find bad addresses normalized by sent attempts.
2. Use `Top Participant Failure Counts by Selected Reason` for raw volume after selecting a reason.

panels.title: Failure Drilldown Guide

panels.description: Extra real sends divided by all user requests. This is direct redundancy cost.
panels.title: Extra Real Sends per User Request

panels.description: No-send or skipped slot burns divided by user requests. This captures scheduling cost before HTTP send.
panels.title: Ghost or No-Send Slots per User Request

panels.description: Suppressed loser terminal attempts divided by user requests. This shows completed work not shown to the user.
panels.title: Suppressed Losers per User Request

panels.description: Extra-attempt reasons that are expected to protect users. High values can justify redundancy but should still guide timeout tuning.
panels.title: Useful Redundancy Reasons

panels.description: Exploration-driven extra attempts. Use this to separate protocol learning cost from failure recovery cost.
panels.title: Exploration Extra Attempts

panels.description: No-send reasons that indicate policy pressure, capability mismatch, or participant health problems rather than useful recovery.
panels.title: Waste or Policy Pressure No-Sends

panels.description: Top skipped/no-send slot reasons in the selected range. Start here, choose a high-volume reason, then use the detail table below.
panels.title: Top Skipped-Slot Reasons

panels.description: Participant and escrow detail for the selected skipped-slot reason. Use this after the top-reasons table identifies what to investigate.

targets.expr: topk(30, sum(increase(devshard_gateway_slot_decisions_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",escrow_id=~"$escrow_id",reason=~"$reason",decision!="real_send"}[$__range])) by (participant_key, model, escrow_id, reason, quarantine_mode))

panels.title: Skipped-Slot Detail for Selected Reason

panels.description: Real no-winner sends by reason and quarantine mode. These participants help availability but should not win unless no clean winner exists.
panels.title: No-Winner Attempts by Reason and Mode

panels.description: Current number of blocked participants within each selected escrow and model. Diagnostic only: use participant tables to identify addresses.
panels.title: Escrow Blocked Participant Count

panels.description: Participants with at least `min_attempts` real sends in the selected range. This is the base volume filter for the quality row.

targets.expr: topk(30, sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Sent Attempts by Participant and Model

panels.description: Successful terminal attempts divided by all terminal attempts for participants above the volume threshold.

targets.expr: topk(30, (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_terminal_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",outcome="success"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_terminal_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1)) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Participant Success Rate

panels.description: Timeout actions by participant and model in the selected range. This is a count table; use the timeout row for reason-first trends.
panels.title: Timeout Actions by Participant

panels.description: No-receipt and empty-stream rates by participant. These are common quarantine inputs.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~"no_receipt|empty_stream"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1))

panels.title: No-Receipt and Empty-Stream Rates

panels.description: Transport and EOF failure rates by participant. These usually point to upstream connectivity or stream truncation.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~"eof_transport|error_stream|transport_error"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1))

panels.title: Transport and EOF Failure Rates

panels.description: Current quarantine or no-winner mode by participant and model. Other participant signals are shown in their own single-purpose panels.
panels.title: Current Participant Quarantine Mode

panels.description: Failure rate by participant and model, normalized by sent attempts and gated by `min_attempts`. Use this before looking at raw failure counts.

targets.expr: topk(30, (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~"$reason"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1)) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Top Participant Failure Rates by Model

panels.description: Raw failure counts after selecting a reason. This is a volume drilldown, not a score.
panels.title: Top Participant Failure Counts by Selected Reason

panels.description: Model x escrow ghost/no-send pressure. High values indicate localized routing, capability, or quarantine pressure.
panels.title: Model x Escrow No-Send Pressure

panels.description: Capacity-aware picker choices by model and escrow. Use this to confirm traffic is flowing to expected escrows.
panels.title: Runtime Picker Choices by Model and Escrow

panels.description: Capability no-send skips by model and participant. This uses the existing bounded slot-decision reason, not the future capability-subreason metric.
panels.title: Capability Skips by Model and Participant

panels.description: Timeout work grouped by kind and action: expected, started, completed, skipped, or failed. Failed or skipped actions should be understood before tuning timeouts.
panels.title: Timeout Actions by Kind

panels.description: Skipped and failed timeout work grouped by action and reason over time. Use this to choose a timeout reason before opening participant detail.
panels.title: Timeout Skip and Failure Reasons Over Time

panels.description: Participant detail for skipped or failed timeout work after a reason is selected. This table intentionally keeps participant detail out of the overview.

targets.expr: topk(30, sum(increase(devshard_gateway_timeout_actions_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",action=~"skipped|failed",reason=~"$reason"}[$__range])) by (participant_key, model, kind, action, reason))

panels.title: Timeout Participant Detail for Selected Reason

panels.description: Cache hit and total request rates. This is diagnostic because cache hits may not carry fresh participant attribution.
panels.title: Cache and Request Lifecycle

panels.description: Participant-bound transport errors by address, model, path kind, and upstream status. Use this for address-level transport investigation.
panels.title: Upstream Transport Errors by Participant

panels.description: Speculative decisions and attempt starts by reason. This explains why the gateway decided to race or explore.
panels.title: Speculative Routing Mechanics

panels.description: Diagnostic runtime active state by selected escrow and model. 1 means the runtime is currently active.
panels.title: Runtime Active State by Escrow

panels.description: Current per-model capacity scale. Scale is current model weight divided by baseline model weight; values below 1 explain lower effective caps.
panels.title: Model Capacity Scale by Model

panels.description: Host transport connection state by remote address. This is network plumbing evidence, not participant scoring.
panels.title: Host Transport Connections

panels.description: Reasons that create extra sends or hidden failures. Use this to tune redundancy and timeout windows by model.
panels.title: Redundancy Pressure by Reason and Model

panels.description: Participants that repeatedly require extra sends. This ranks one signal only; use with redundancy pressure before tuning timeout or redundancy policy.
panels.title: Participants Requiring Extra Sends

panels.description: Participants with no-winner pressure. These addresses can help availability but should not normally provide the final answer.
panels.title: Participants with No-Winner Pressure

panels.description: Participants entering quarantine or no-winner modes. Use this to tune strike thresholds and quarantine policy.
panels.title: Participants Entering Quarantine or No-Winner Modes

panels.description: Current and baseline capacity weights by selected model. Escrow load and blocked participants are split into diagnostic panels with their own units.
panels.title: Model Capacity Weights by Model

panels.description: Participant-budget rejects ranked by address, model, and routing scope. `participant_key="unknown"` means the gateway only knew an escrow-level capacity failure.
panels.title: Participant-Budget Rejections by Participant and Model

panels.description: Range count of attributed user-visible winners by participant and model. Use with winner share to distinguish dominance from low volume.
panels.title: User-Visible Winner Count by Participant

panels.description: 1 means at least one participant budget currently limits the selected escrow. Diagnostic only; use participant rejection tables for address attribution.
panels.title: Escrow Participant Budget Limited State

panels.description: Failure share by participant, model, and reason, normalized by sent attempts and gated by `min_attempts`.

targets.expr: topk(30, (sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~"$reason"}[$__range])) / ignoring(reason) group_left clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1)) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Participant Failed Sends per Sent Attempt

panels.description: Failed sent attempts divided by attributed user-visible wins for each participant and model. High values mean redundancy hides costly failures.

targets.expr: topk(30, (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~"$reason"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_user_visible_wins_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1)) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Participant Failed Sends per Visible Win

panels.description: Suppressed loser failures ranked by participant and reason. These did not reach the user but still consumed participant work.
panels.title: Hidden Loser Failures by Participant

panels.description: Quarantine-driven no-send slots by participant and model. Use this to find addresses changing scheduling before HTTP send.
panels.title: Skipped Quarantine Slots by Participant

panels.description: Skipped or failed timeout work divided by sent attempts for each participant and model. Use after selecting a timeout reason.

targets.expr: topk(30, (sum by (participant_key, model, kind, action, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_timeout_actions_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",action=~"skipped|failed",reason=~"$reason"}[$__range])) / ignoring(kind, action, reason) group_left clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1)))

panels.title: Timeout Skipped or Failed by Participant

panels.description: Current active request count by selected escrow and model.
panels.title: Runtime Active Requests by Escrow

panels.description: Current reserved input tokens by selected escrow and model.
panels.title: Runtime Reserved Tokens by Escrow

panels.description: Per-escrow effective picker weight W(e). Use with runtime and blocked-participant panels to assess sizing pressure.
panels.title: Escrow Sizing Pressure Summary
